title: Erdős's distinct subset sums conjecture
formal: Does there exist an absolute real constant \(c>0\) such that, for every integer \(n\ge1\) and every increasing sequence of positive integers \(a_1<\cdots<a_n\) with all \(2^n\) subset sums distinct, one has \(a_n\ge c\,2^n\)?
definitions: For a subset S of {1,...,n}, its subset sum is \(\sum_{i\in S}a_i\), with empty sum zero. Distinctness means that different subsets always produce different sums. The single constant c must work for every sequence and every n. A sequence of counterexamples would have to make \(a_n/2^n\) arbitrarily small; one unusually efficient finite example alone does not refute the assertion.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof or refutation of the stated proposition, with all its quantifiers and hypotheses. Verification of finitely many parameter values does not establish the universal assertion.
why: How economically can binary choices be encoded by adding integer weights? This is an extremal counterpart of subset-sum encoding.

context_blocks.text: Powers of two provide an immediate construction at the conjectured exponential scale. The difficulty is the uniform positive factor in the lower bound.
Steinerberger gives an analytic perspective on the problem and the known lower-bound scale with an additional square-root loss. That loss is precisely what the conjecture removes.
